statement: A rectangular enclosure is made using $100$ m of fencing on three sides, the fourth side being an existing wall. Find the maximum possible area.
solution:
Let the two sides perpendicular to the wall have length $x$ and the side parallel to the wall have length $y$. Then $2x+y=100$, so $y=100-2x$.
The area is $A=xy=x(100-2x)=100x-2x^{2}$.
$$\frac{dA}{dx}=100-4x,$$
which is zero when $x=25$; then $y=50$. The second derivative is $-4<0$, confirming a maximum.
The maximum area is $25\times50=1250\,\text{m}^{2}$.
hints: Express the fenced length as 2x + y = 100.
Write area A in terms of a single variable.
